title: Batch Accountant: Prefill Inspector and Quant Profile Linter (CLI)
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Customers and internal SREs repeatedly ask for a repeatable way to audit prefill/batching defaults and validate quantization profiles against tenant unit-econ expectations. This PR adds a small, focused CLI (batch-accountant) that inspects runtime prefill/batching defaults, lints quant profiles for common pitfalls (e.g., incompatible precision knobs, excessively aggressive layer folding), and produces a per-tenant unit-economics summary to help ops teams choose safe defaults. || What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new CLI command `redwood batch-accountant inspect` that queries the config store and serves a human-readable audit plus CSV export for downstream chargeback / finance tooling. 2) Adds a quant-profile linter that flags unsupported combinations and suggests safe fallbacks (e.g., fallback to q4_0 for specific attention layers). 3) Implements a conservative unit-econ estimator that simulates per-token cost under a set of representative sequence-length percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and batch shape assumptions. 4) Patches runtime config lookup to expose prefill / cache hint metadata to the inspector. 5) Adds integration tests and telemetry hooks (prefill.audit.executed, quant.lint.warn-count). || Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-2147) - [x] Unit tests for linter - [x] Integration test exercising CLI against a local config snapshot - [x] Docs: CLI usage + examples - [x] Telemetry events instrumented - [x] Safety: default linter severity = warn (no automatic rewrites) || Commits (high-level): - Add batch-accountant CLI scaffolding and command dispatch - Implement config introspector and CSV exporter - Implement quant-profile linter and ruleset v1 - Add unit-econ estimator module and test harness - Wire telemetry and add prometheus counters - Add docs and examples - Fix lint issues from CI run || Files changed (high level): - cmd/batch_accountant/main.go (CLI entrypoint, flags parsing, CSV export) - internal/inspector/config_reader.go (reads prefill/caching metadata) - internal/lint/quant_linter.go (ruleset, rule definitions) - internal/econ/estimator.go (unit-econ simulator) - tests/integration/batch_accountant_test.go - docs/ops/batch-accountant.md - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new counters) - go.mod / go.sum updates for csv writer library || CI history: Initial CI run (2026-02-19) failed on golangci-lint (unused variable introduced in estimator). I pushed a follow-up commit to address lint and added a CI-only test to ensure telemetry counters are registered (prevents flakiness in integration). Second CI run passed all checks including unit, integration, and e2e smoke. Build matrix: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, go1.20. || Review timeline and conversation (summarized): Marcus: "Nice focused tool — can we make sure the CSV column names are stable? finance will rely on them." Author: "CSV schema is versioned; added a header 'schema_version' and included a short example in docs." Priya: "Quant linter rules look good; please add an opt-out flag for tenants that run experimental quant libs." Author: "Added --allow-experimental to the CLI and documented behavior; linter remains warn-by-default." Evan: "Unit-econ estimator uses a few assumptions — can we make the percentiles configurable?" Author: "Exposed --p50 --p90 --p99 flags with defaults matching production telemetry distribution. Added tests covering non-default flags." Marcus (approval): "Approved after one minor doc tweak." Priya (approval): "Approved." Evan (approval): "Approved." || Safety notes: Linter defaults to warn only and does not mutate configuration. The CLI requires operator privileges to access tenant configs; a non-privileged user will receive a clear permission error. Telemetry events were reviewed by security for PII leakage and pass the audit (only emits numeric counters and hashed tenant ids). || Merge outcome: Squash merge performed on 2026-03-03. Release note: see release_notes field. || How to use (short): `redwood batch-accountant inspect --tenant TENANT_ID --out report.csv --allow-experimental` will write a CSV and print a short unit-econ summary to stdout. || Related: ENG-2147 (design), ENG-3301 (tenant audit playbook).
release_notes: Add batch-accountant CLI to audit prefill/batching defaults and lint quant profiles (warn-only by default)
Expose per-tenant unit-economics estimator and CSV export for finance/ops
Telemetry: prefill.audit.executed and quant.lint.warn-count counters added
